item.title: Tiger Shroff shooting suspects travel 4km before escaping on foot
item.description:
Three men suspected of firing at actor Tiger Shroff’s car in Mumbai’s Juhu area on Sunday evening reportedly traveled about 4km on a motorcycle before abandoning it near a police beat post in Andheri and fleeing on foot.
The shooting took place around 7pm near Pushpa Park, about 100 meters from Juhu police station. Five rounds were reportedly fired at Shroff’s BMW as he returned home after playing football. The actor was not shot, but his driver and another person near the vehicle were injured.
According to preliminary reports, three men arrived on a motorcycle. Two allegedly opened fire while the third assisted their escape. The suspects reportedly rode toward Andheri railway station, passing several busy junctions, including those near Mithibai College and SV Road.
They abandoned the motorcycle outside a police beat post before crossing the railway bridge toward the eastern side of the station. Police recovered the motorcycle around 9pm and took it to DN Nagar police station.
Investigators are examining closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage to trace the suspects’ movements and identify any vehicle they may have used afterward. Police have formed 15 teams to investigate the shooting, and the case is expected to be transferred to the Crime Branch.
A social media post attributed to Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu claimed responsibility for the attack on behalf of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang. However, police have not confirmed the authenticity of the post or established the gang’s involvement.
The incident has drawn comparisons with previous attacks in Mumbai linked to the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, including the October 2024 murder of politician Baba Siddique and shootings outside the residences of actor Salman Khan and filmmaker Rohit Shetty.
Investigators have yet to establish whether the latest shooting is connected to those incidents.
Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde visited Shroff’s residence after the shooting and assured the family of government support. Shinde condemned the incident and said to the indian media outlets: “No form of threat will be tolerated.”
Shroff’s mother, Ayesha Shroff, briefly responded to questions about her son from India Today by giving a thumbs-up and saying: “God is great.”
The investigation is ongoing, and further details may emerge as police examine the evidence.

item.title: BTMA calls for data-driven policy to protect textile industry
item.description:
The Bangladesh Textile Mills Association (BTMA) has called for the formulation of data-driven policies to ensure the protection, fair competition, and export competitiveness of the primary textile sector, particularly the spinning industry.
This information was shared in a press release signed by BTMA Secretary General Zakir Hossain on Sunday (October 18).
The release clarified that no new tariffs or import bans have been imposed through the withdrawal of bonded warehouse facilities on the import of 10–30 count cotton yarn.
The requirement of bank guarantees for such imports is primarily intended to protect state revenue and prevent the misuse of trade privileges.
Highlighting the sector's $22 billion investment in spinning mills, the BTMA stated that reopening closed mills and generating new employment opportunities in this industry can play a positive role in recovering bank loans and boosting the national economy.
It added that ensuring imported yarn is used strictly for authorized purposes can be accomplished through bank guarantees, digital surveillance, and risk-based audits.
Consequently, this will reduce the risk of unauthorized leakage of duty-free goods into the local market.
Regarding concerns over the shifting of buyer orders, the association emphasized that international buyers do not make order decisions based on yarn prices alone.
Factors such as quality, technology, productivity, and the ability to ensure timely delivery are equally critical.
To address the situation, the BTMA requested the continuation of the bank guarantee-based import system for 10–30 English count yarn.
Additionally, it proposed enforcing a condition requiring 30% local value addition on raw material imports for non-bonded industries.

item.title: Ficci: Energy reforms, domestic exploration and renewables to boost investment in BD
item.description:
The Foreign Investors’ Chamber of Commerce and Industry (Ficci) has called for urgent reforms, increased domestic gas exploration, and accelerated investment in renewable energy to strengthen Bangladesh’s energy security, improve industrial competitiveness, and attract long-term investment.
The call came at a high-level luncheon meeting titled “Sustainable Power and Energy: Driving Investment in Bangladesh,” held Monday in Dhaka to discuss the country’s energy challenges and identify practical solutions for a reliable, affordable, and sustainable energy future.
The meeting was graced by Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury, MP, Minister for Finance and Planning, as chief guest.
Shafiqul Alam, lead analyst, Bangladesh Energy, South Asia, Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis (IEEFA), delivered the keynote address.
The panel discussion was moderated by Mahbub ur Rahman, CEO, HSBC Bangladesh and former director of the Ficci board, and featured Shu Xiong, president and managing director, Chevron Bangladesh; Prof Mohammad Tamim, vice chancellor, Independent University, Bangladesh; Nazneen Ahmed, executive director, Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD); and Fazlul Hoque, administrator, FBCCI.
Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury, MP acknowledged the significant energy and economic challenges facing Bangladesh, noting that the government had been addressing an energy crisis alongside inherited financial liabilities and structural weaknesses.
He expressed confidence that the economy, including the energy sector, would begin to stabilize by the second year of the government’s tenure, with stronger growth expected in the following years.
He emphasized the need to reduce the cost of doing business, improve the investment climate and strengthen the competitiveness of domestic industries through reforms and deregulation.
The Minister further underscored the importance of comprehensive reforms in taxation, banking and capital markets to restore confidence and facilitate investment.
Referring to plans to separate the National Board of Revenue’s policy-making and enforcement functions, he said the government was pursuing measures to improve efficiency, transparency and accountability.
He called on the private sector to work collaboratively with the government through this transition, expressing optimism that ongoing reforms and investment initiatives would strengthen macroeconomic stability, improve the business environment and support Bangladesh’s long-term economic growth.
Ficci president Rupali Haque Chowdhury highlighted how global energy disruptions have exposed Bangladesh’s vulnerability to imported fuels, raising industrial costs, disrupting production, and creating uncertainty for businesses.
She stressed that energy security must go beyond ensuring supply to making energy reliable, affordable, and sustainable. She called for stronger domestic gas exploration, diversified LNG sourcing, modernized infrastructure, improved energy efficiency, and faster renewable energy investment.
She also underscored the importance of regional cooperation and greater private-sector participation in building a resilient energy system to support industrial growth, export diversification, and job creation.
Delivering the keynote, Shafiqul Alam highlighted Bangladesh’s growing energy challenges, driven by declining domestic gas reserves, rising LNG imports, and volatile global fuel prices.
He noted that domestic gas reserves could be depleted by 2036 without new discoveries, increasing pressure on power generation costs, industrial competitiveness, and household affordability.
During the panel discussion, the speakers highlighted the need for stronger domestic gas exploration, investment-friendly policies, and a diversified energy mix to ensure energy security and affordability.
Shu Xiong stressed the importance of a stable regulatory environment to attract long-term foreign investment, while Prof Mohammad Tamim emphasized balancing domestic gas production with renewable energy.
Fazlul Hoque highlighted the impact of energy shortages and rising costs on industrial productivity and investment, calling for greater support for rooftop solar and green financing.
Nazneen Ahmed underscored the importance of attracting foreign investment while maintaining fiscal sustainability and affordable energy.
Ficci board director Shadab Ahmed Khan delivered the vote of thanks.

item.title: Loan disbursement for reviving closed industries go slow
item.description:
Despite Bangladesh Bank's announcement of a Tk 62,000 crore stimulus package to reopen closed factories, generate new employment, and revitalize the economy, progress in loan disbursement remains sluggish.
Over the past five months, entrepreneurs have received only Tk561 crore out of the Tk20,000 crore allocated for closed industrial and service sectors.
This means less than 3% of the sector's total allocation has been disbursed, raising doubts about achieving the goals of reopening closed factories and creating jobs.
According to Bangladesh Bank data, loan disbursements worth another Tk929.50 crore for closed industrial and service sectors are currently being processed.
As a result, a major portion of the allocation remains beyond the reach of entrepreneurs.
Across the entire stimulus package, a total of Tk11,959.82 crore has been disbursed so far from 15 separate funds.
Additionally, loan processing for another Tk2,560 crore is underway. Combining both disbursed and in-process funds, the total comes to Tk14,519.79 crore—meaning less than one-fifth of the total Tk62,000 crore package has been distributed.
Under this package, the maximum interest rate on loans is set at 7%, with the remaining interest subsidized by the government.
The initiative aims to create employment for 2.5 million people.
Data from Bangladesh Bank shows that the highest amount, Tk6,917 crore, was disbursed from the pre-shipment credit refinance scheme.
A special fund for cottage and micro-entrepreneurs disbursed Tk 2,500 crore, while approximately Tk908 crore was disbursed as working capital for small and medium enterprises (SMEs).
Furthermore, Tk500 crore was disbursed to the creative economy, Tk293 crore to agricultural and rural economic activities, and Tk200 crore to foreign employment generation.
Business owners and bankers point to mutual constraints for the slow pace of loan disbursement.
Businesspersons allege that while loans are urgently needed to restart closed factories, banks are reluctant to extend financing.
Securing new loans has become difficult due to issues surrounding collateral and previous loan defaults.
However, they argue that once factories reopen, production and sales will increase, gradually enabling them to repay the loans.
Additionally, per a July 29 directive from Bangladesh Bank, applicants must withdraw ongoing lawsuits against the government, Bangladesh Bank, or the relevant financial institution before receiving special policy support.
Entrepreneurs expressed uncertainty, as there is no guarantee of obtaining a loan even after withdrawing their cases.
On the other hand, bankers state that amid high non-performing loan (NPL) pressures, they must carefully verify the applicant's financial standing, collateral, and the feasibility of restarting the factory before issuing new loans. This naturally prolongs the approval process.
Business owners have demanded relaxed loan conditions, faster application processing, and priority for factories with high potential for production and job creation.
They also suggested that banks provide written in-principle approval before requiring the withdrawal of pending lawsuits.

item.title: Apollo Hospitals Chennai holds Int’l CME Program for Doctors at Apollo Clinic Dhanmondi
item.description:
Apollo Hospitals, Teynampet, Chennai, in collaboration with Apollo Clinic, Dhanmondi, Dhaka (licensed by JMI Specialized Hospital PLC), organized an International Continuing Medical Education (CME) program for doctors.
The initiative aimed to facilitate advanced knowledge sharing and foster professional development in specialized cancer care.
The day commenced with an awareness rally and a celebratory cake-cutting ceremony to mark Breast Cancer Awareness Month, observed globally throughout October.
Approximately 100 Bangladeshi medical students, postgraduate residents, and specialist consultants attended the program to exchange clinical insights with leading international experts in medical oncology, gastroenterology, gynecology, and breast oncoplastic surgery.
Held at the premises of Apollo Clinic, Dhanmondi, the CME featured two key specialized sessions: “Beyond Chemotherapy: The Evolving Role of Immunotherapy and Targeted Therapy in Breast, Lung, and Colorectal Cancer” and “Evolving Paradigms in the Management of Breast Cancer.”
The keynote presentations were delivered by Dr Niranjan Vijayaraghavan, an experienced medical oncologist at Apollo Hospitals, Teynampet, Chennai, and Dr Usha Gautam Mehta, renowned specialist in gastroenterology, gynecology, and breast oncology.
Representing Apollo Clinic, Dhanmondi, Dr Ali Nafisa, a leading oncoplastic and breast surgeon, also delivered insightful remarks highlighting the critical importance of specialized breast care and timely cancer awareness.
The program was conducted under the leadership of Dr Tamjeed Alam, CEO of Apollo Clinic, Dhanmondi.
The event was attended by Ragil Raghunath, deputy general manager (DGM) of International Business, representing Apollo Hospitals, Teynampet, Chennai.
Also representing Apollo Clinic, Dhanmondi, were adviser Mosiur Rahman Kamal; directors Dr Saiful Islam and Dr Adnan Ahmed; director of Medical Services Brigadier General (Retd.) Dr Shafiqul Islam; and chief operating officer (COO) Md Papul Mia.
This CME program further strengthens the growing strategic collaboration between JMI Specialized Hospital PLC, one of Bangladesh's premier healthcare providers, and the Apollo Hospitals Group, a globally renowned South Asian healthcare network operating more than 76 hospitals and 700+ clinics across multiple countries.
The partnership aims to provide Bangladeshi patients with reliable, world-class healthcare services locally at an affordable cost—significantly reducing the need to seek treatment abroad, advancing the country's healthcare ecosystem, and positioning Bangladesh as an emerging destination for medical tourism.
During the event, Apollo Clinic Dhanmondi highlighted several of its key clinical achievements to date, including serving more than 22,000 outpatients (OPD), managing over 2,500 inpatient (IPD) cases, and successfully performing more than 1,000 surgical procedures.
Demonstrating its uncompromising commitment to patient safety and quality care, the clinic proudly reported a surgical site infection (SSI) rate of less than 1%.

item.title: Fast celebrates ‘World Bread and Ban Day’ for the first time in Bangladesh
item.description:
For the first time in Bangladesh, "World Bread and Ban Day" was celebrated with great splendor. Akij Bakers Limited's popular brand, Fast Bread and Bun, organized this historic event at "The Grandeur" located in Suvastu Hena Skyline, Gulshan, Dhaka.
Numerous bread and bun enthusiasts from across the country participated in this colorful festival, which ran from 3:00 PM to 8:00 PM.
The main attraction of the event was a special "Live Sandwich Creation Station" for the attending guests.
A wide variety of different flavored premium ingredients were provided there. Visitors enjoyed the exceptional experience of making sandwiches using their own recipes with ingredients of their choice.
The event commenced with Sheikh Jamil Uddin, managing director of Akij Bakers Limited, cutting a giant-sized bun alongside the invited guests.
The organizers stated that Fast Bread and Bun has earned the distinction of being the first brand in Bangladesh to officially celebrate this day.
This unique initiative was undertaken to highlight the involvement and nutritional importance of bread and bun in modern, busy lives, and such efforts will continue in the future.
The event was attended by Sheikh Jamil Uddin, managing director of Akij Bakers Limited, along with other senior officials of the company.

item.title: NCC Bank launches ‘China Desk’ to strengthen banking services for Chinese businesses
item.description:
With the aim of providing integrated banking services to Chinese business enterprises and investors operating in Bangladesh, NCC Bank PLC has launched a specialized China Desk named ‘NCC China Connect’.
The main objective of this initiative is to accelerate bilateral trade, investment and business growth between Bangladesh and China.
The China Desk was inaugurated on Wednesday, October 14, at the ‘China National Day Celebration 2026’ held at the Grand Ballroom of Radisson Blu Hotel, Dhaka, organized by the Bangladesh China Chamber of Commerce and Industry (BCCCI) in collaboration with NCC Bank.
The event was held on the occasion of the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People’s Republic of China.
The chief guest at the event was State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam, MP.
Special guest was Liu Yuyin, Chargé d’Affaires of the Embassy of the People’s Republic of China in Bangladesh.
Members of BCCCI, chairman of NCC Bank Mohammed Nurun Newaz Salim, vice-chairman Abdus Salam, director & past chairman Amjadul Ferdous Chowdhury, director & chairman of the executive committee Khairul Alam Chaklader, director Md Moinuddin, director Mohammed Sazzad Un Newaz, director & past vice-chairman Tanzina Ali, directors Syed Asif Nizamuddin, Shamima Newaz, Morshedul Alam Chaklader, Nahid Banu, independent director Meer Sajed-Ul-Basher, and independent director & chairman of the audit committee Md Amirul Islam.
Managing director M Shamsul Arefin, additional managing director M Khurshed Alam, Md Zakir Anam & Mohammed Jamal Uddin Mazumder, deputy managing directors Mohammed Mizanur Rahman & Md Habibur Rahman along with senior officials of the bank and leaders of Chinese businesses in Bangladesh also attended.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam, MP, highlighted the importance of Bangladesh-China relations in expanding trade, investment and economic cooperation.
She expressed hope that initiatives such as NCC Bank’s China Desk would facilitate business activities between the two countries and further strengthen bilateral economic relations.
Special guest Liu Yuyin welcomed the initiative to launch a specialized banking platform for Chinese business enterprises in Bangladesh. He hoped that this Desk would play a role in expanding bilateral trade and investment, increasing business connectivity and further strengthening the economic partnership between Bangladesh and China.
NCC Bank chairman Mohammad Nurun Newaz Salim said that the launch of the China Desk reflected the bank’s commitment to supporting Chinese business enterprises and expanding bilateral trade and investment between Bangladesh and China.
NCC Bank managing director M Shamsul Arefin said: “China is Bangladesh’s largest trading partner and one of the most important sources of investment. Through ‘NCC China Connect’, we want to provide integrated and specialized banking services to Chinese business enterprises, which will accelerate trade, investment and sustainable growth between the two countries. Operated under our Multinational Corporate Banking Division, this Desk will serve as a central point of contact for Chinese entrepreneurs. Through it, along with support in Mandarin, various services will be provided, including trade finance, working capital, project financing, foreign exchange transactions, bank guarantees, cash management and digital banking. Using correspondent banking relationships with 30 banks in China and a network of nearly 400 correspondent banks worldwide, we are committed to facilitating and expediting cross-border foreign trade transaction settlement with China. In addition, we are also working to create opportunities for Chinese trade transactions settlement in the Chinese currency Renminbi (RMB).”

item.title: Home Ministry to form committees in all upazilas to curb juvenile gangs
item.description:
The Home Ministry has decided to form committees in all upazilas across the country to curb juvenile gang activities.
The respective upazila nirbahi officer (UNO) will serve as chairperson, while the officer-in-charge (OC) of the local police station will be the member secretary.
The decision was announced in a statement signed by Home Ministry Public Relations Officer Faisal Hasan on Monday.
The initiative aims to coordinate the efforts of local administrations and police to prevent juvenile gang activities at the grassroots level, Faisal said.
However, the ministry did not disclose the names or positions of other committee members, the activities they will undertake, or a deadline for forming the committees.

item.title: IUB, Mutual Trust Bank hold MTO recruitment roadshow
item.description:
Independent University, Bangladesh (IUB), in collaboration with Mutual Trust Bank PLC (MTB), organized the “Pathways to Leadership” Roadshow 2026 at the university’s DMK Lecture Gallery on October 13, 2026.
The event was organized by IUB’s Office of Career Guidance, Placement & Alumni Relations (CGP&AR) to familiarize students with MTB’s upcoming recruitment process for Management Trainee Officer (MTO) positions and help them prepare for the selection process.
Representatives from MTB explained the application procedure, examination stages, preparation strategies, and the benefits and career development opportunities offered through the bank’s management trainee program.
A K M Tareq, deputy managing director and head of the Branch Banking Division at MTB, and Sharmin Akhter, head of recruitment at the bank’s Group Human Resources department, attended as speakers. They shared insights into the recruitment process, expectations of prospective candidates, and professional opportunities available to successful applicants.
Md Wasim Jabber, MCIPS, treasurer of IUB, delivered the welcome address. He highlighted the importance of connecting students directly with employers and equipping them with practical knowledge to pursue corporate career opportunities.
The roadshow provided students with information on applying for MTB’s MTO positions and preparing for recruitment examinations, helping them make informed decisions about pursuing careers in the banking sector.
The initiative reflects IUB’s continued commitment to strengthening industry-academia collaboration and creating opportunities for students to engage directly with prospective employers.

item.title: Pakistan envoy, opposition leader discuss West Asia conflict
item.description:
Pakistan High Commissioner Imran Haider met Bangladesh’s Leader of the Opposition Shafiqur Rahman on Monday, discussing the West Asia conflict, regional developments and bilateral relations between the two countries.
During the meeting, Shafiqur Rahman appreciated Pakistan’s peacebuilding efforts to resolve the conflict in West Asia. He emphasized the need for sustained dialogue and diplomacy to end the war and alleviate the suffering of affected people.
Haider reiterated Pakistan’s commitment to peace in the region and beyond, thanking the opposition leader for the exchange.
He also briefed Shafiqur Rahman on the progress of bilateral cooperation in health, education, trade, culture and people-to-people contacts.
Both sides expressed satisfaction with the positive momentum in Pakistan-Bangladesh relations.

item.title: Hurzeler lauds Gomez after Brighton goal from halfway line
item.description:
Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler praised the inspirational Diego Gomez after his goal from the halfway line set the stage for a 5-0 thrashing of Crystal Palace in the Premier League on Sunday.
Paraguay midfielder Gomez was on target for the first time this season in spectacular fashion at the Amex Stadium.
He left Palace goalkeeper Walter Benitez red-faced with a sensational shot that arrowed into the net from just inside the Palace half.
The 51-metre goal of the season contender evoked memories of David Beckham's astonishing effort against Wimbledon from a similar distance 30 years ago.
Gomez's wonder-strike was the longest Premier League goal since Wayne Rooney scored from 58 metres for Everton against West Ham in 2017.
Gomez had been well off target with a similar attempt during last weekend's 2-0 win at Sunderland.
But Hurzeler credited him for trying again, while also showing the mentality the Albion boss craves.
"He's a hard worker, he always puts the team first. He's always 'we' then 'me'," Hurzeler said.
"I know how desperately he wants to get involved in scoring and having assists.
"Last week, he showed against Sunderland, there was already that attempt shooting from the halfway line. There the wind wasn't perfect for this try. Now the wind was better for him.
"I'm really happy that he gets this reward for all of the effort he's putting into the club, into his own development, and into the team."
Jaydee Canvot's own goal set Brighton on course for a fourth successive top-flight win before Yasin Ayari's deflected finish quickly added to Gomez's stunner in a remarkable opening 10 minutes.
Charalampos Kostoulas and Jack Hinshelwood struck in the second half to equal Albion's biggest win over Palace.
The result also secured Hurzeler's first victory over Palace, taking his third-placed Seagulls to 16 points from seven games.
It was a sweet moment for the German, who was subjected to chants of "you're getting sacked in the morning" from angry Brighton supporters during a 1-0 home defeat by Palace in February.
"The last game against Palace made me really grounded, having this criticism it wasn't easy," he said.
"And now we sit here in a completely different mood, with a feeling of being really proud.
"It's just a privilege to be part of this group and therefore I'm really pleased and happy for everyone who is part of this club.
"I hope everyone enjoys the night today; it's a much better night than a few months ago and a much better feeling."

item.title: 'Surprise package' Lazio crush Juve to move level with Serie A leaders Inter
item.description:
Lazio scored a statement win on Sunday, brushing aside Juventus 3-0 in Turin to move level on points with Inter Milan at the top of Serie A.
Lazio trail the defending champions on goal difference, but 19 points is their highest total after seven league games, surpassing the 17 accumulated by Sven Goran Ericsson's team to open the 1999-2000 season.
That side went unbeaten for their first nine games and ended up winning their second, and most recent, Serie A title, by one point from Juventus.
"We may well be the surprise package of this league, but we mustn't change our approach, we need to take each match as it comes and work hard," said Lazio coach Gennaro Gattuso.
Lazio took control with a Danish double.
Oliver Provstgaard, a 1.93m centre back, leapt high above the home defence after 37 minutes and guided a header inside the far post.
After 66 minutes, winger Gustav Isaksen, faced by a backpedalling fullback, drifted inside and placed a low shot inside the far post.
With three minutes left, substitute Fisayo Dele-Bashiru picked up the ball in his own half and cantered unhindered into the Juventus penalty area before sliding home his shot.
Juventus, who were booed off by their fans, have won just one of their last five league matches and are eighth, eight points adrift.
"We were clearly outplayed, we were slow, we lacked ideas," said coach Luciano Spalletti. "It's hard to understand."
- 'Right balance' -
AC Milan held off visiting Atalanta 3-2 to end the weekend fourth, four points off the lead.
Young Slovenian Relja Obric made a nightmare debut for Atalanta.
The 20-year-old came on for injured Sead Kolasinac after 19 minutes but his first touch in Serie A five minutes later was a handball as he instinctively moved his arm into the path of a shot from Yunus Musah.
Milan's club-record signing Goncalo Ramos placed the penalty inside Marco Carnesecchi's left-hand post.
Then Obric allowed a shot from France midfielder Adrien Rabiot through his legs as Milan doubled their lead before half-time.
Danish central defender Thomas Kristensen gave away a carbon copy handball penalty after 65 minutes. Ramos went the other way but Carnesecchi saved it.
The reprieve was short-lived. Rabiot nodded on the corner and Mario Gila headed in from point-blank range at the far post.
Gianluca Gaetano and Nikola Krstovic pulled two back for the visitors in the second half but it was too little, too late for Atalanta as they succumbed to a fourth defeat of the campaign.
"Usually, we struggle at the start of the match and play better in the second half. It was the opposite today; we need to find the right balance, but these are three important points in our season," said Rabiot.
Como won 3-1 at struggling Fiorentina to rise to fifth.
First-half goals by Mattia Liberali and Nico Paz put Como in charge, before Marin Pongracic halved the deficit shortly before the interval.
Anastasios Douvikas netted early in the second period to keep the hosts locked in the relegation zone on four points.
For Como, it was a first win in four matches, going back over the international break to mid-September.
"We played a very complete game," coach Cesc Fabregas said. "There are risks when you play the way we do. There's no such thing as perfect tactics."
Earlier, Lecce won 3-0 at Udinese, with Kialonda Gaspar, Konan N'Dri and Jamil Siebert all finding the net.

item.title: Lyon go top of Ligue 1 as Monaco fall to first defeat of the season
item.description:
Ten-man Lyon held on for a come-from-behind 2-1 victory over Nice to move top of Ligue 1 on Sunday, as previous pace-setters Monaco lost for the first time this season.
Five teams are level on 14 points at the top of the table with Lyon heading Paris Saint-Germain, Paris FC, Lille and Monaco on goal difference.
Lyon head to PSG next weekend.
"It's good to be top but it's not the most important thing," said Lyon coach Paulo Fonseca.
"But having 14 points is very positive. Of course, that gives us confidence and greater responsibilities, but at this stage of the season it changes nothing."
It was a close run affair for Lyon, playing in front of local boy and French cycling prodigy Paul Seixas, following Keito Nakamura's dismissal 20 minutes from time.
Ivory Coast forward Elye Wahi, who opened the scoring for Nice on 18 minutes with his second goal of the season, was denied an injury-time equaliser by a razor-tight offside call.
Two goals in three minutes turned the game around by half-time as Pavel Sulc equalised by prodding home a rebound and Tanner Tessmann headed the hosts in front.
Veteran Belgium midfielder Axel Witsel headed against the bar early in the second half while Wahi hit the post with a close-range header, shortly after Nakamura was dismissed for a high boot.
Noah Cadiou's second-half penalty for Lorient prevented Monaco from returning to the top of Ligue 1 as the principality outfit fell to a 1-0 defeat in Brittany on Sunday.
Wing back Dembo Sylla earned the penalty on the hour mark at the Stade du Moustoir as he was felled by Monaco captain Denis Zakaria.
Finnish goalkeeper Lukas Hradecky dived the right way, but Cadiou placed his spot-kick into the corner, to hand Monaco their first league defeat of the season.
Paris FC joined the leading quintet as Lassine Sinayoko's injury-time penalty gave them a 4-3 victory over Rennes, who dropped to fifth, a point behind the leading five, despite forward Esteban Lepaul's hat-trick of penalties.
Maxime Lopez twice gave the hosts the lead, only for Lepaul, who earned his first France cap in the recent international window, to equalise from the spot.
Lassine Sinayoko looked to have given PFC the victory 14 minutes from time with a stunning overhead bicycle kick, only for Brazilian substitute Otavio's clumsy handball to hand Lepaul the chance to level up a third time.
But Sinayoko had the last word, drilling home his penalty after VAR intervened to punish Valentin Rongier's shirt tug on the Mali forward.
Marseille picked up a much-needed win as they thumped Angers 5-2 to pull away from the relegation zone.
Lilian Raolisoa gave Angers the lead but Marseille replied with goals before half-time from Himad Abdelli and Nouhoum Kamissoko.
Amine Gouiri scored his fifth goal of the season for Marseille when he tucked home the rebound after his penalty was saved by Anthony Lopes.
Amine El Ouazzani struck from the spot to pull a goal back for Angers but late efforts from Amine Harit and Igor Paixao wrapped up just a third win in seven league matches for Marseille.
Bruno Genesio's side began the weekend above the relegation play-off spot only on goal difference, having also lost their first two games in the Europa League.
Winless Le Havre remain rooted to the foot of the table as Cameroon forward Danny Namaso's brace helped Auxerre come away from Normandy with a 3-1 victory and put daylight between themselves and the relegation zone.

item.title: Mbappe hits two as Real Madrid rout Sevilla
item.description:
Kylian Mbappe scored twice including one brilliant individual goal as Real Madrid thrashed Sevilla 4-1 on Sunday to climb into third in La Liga.
Arda Guler, who was fortunate to avoid an early red card for an elbow, netted a spectacular opener before Mbappe's double and a rocket from Yan Diomande as Jose Mourinho side moved above Real Betis.
Mbappe's first was a sensational strike, involving a roulette on the edge of Sevilla's box, and his second a chipped Panenka penalty.
Champions Barca are six points ahead of Real Madrid before next weekend's Clasico at Camp Nou after thrashing Betis on Saturday, with Atletico Madrid second, sandwiched between Spain's giants.
"We played a great game... we are a team and we work to improve, we've only been together for a very short time," Mourinho told Real Madrid TV.
"It's hard to have the calm that other coaches enjoy at other clubs, given the scale of Real Madrid, but we're making the most of every minute we have."
Mourinho lined up with Diomande on the left in place of suspended Brazilian winger Vinicius Junior, and brought Guler in as part of the midfield pivot.
Vinicius's red card for hair-pulling last weekend provoked ire in the Spanish capital at officiating in Spain.
Madrid fans at their Santiago Bernabeu stadium chanted and held up banners against La Liga president Javier Tebas, after he said the club's strategy of trying to discredit referees was similar to the techniques of Nazi propaganda chief Joseph Goebbels.
Los Blancos and their new coach Mourinho have complained bitterly about Spanish refereeing in recent weeks, and more generally over the past two seasons, in which they have failed to win a major trophy.
On this occasion it was Sevilla who had more to complain about in terms of officiating as Madrid eased to victory.
A quiet start was disrupted when Madrid midfielder Guler appeared to elbow Sevilla's Peque, which went unpunished midway through the first half.
"There's a match that's 11 against 11 where they deserve to win, without any doubt, but we were denied the chance to play another match," said upset Sevilla coach Luis Garcia Plaza.
"We were denied the chance to play a match of 11 against 10. From there on I don't want to talk about the match anymore. We should have been playing 11 against 10 from the 25th minute."
The coach said "maybe" Guler was not dismissed so Madrid did "not arrive nine points behind" Barca at the Clasico next weekend.
Mourinho said he had seen no replays of the incident which proved Guler had elbowed Peque.
Sevilla had resisted the probing of Madrid's attacking stars early on, but were undone by a moment of magic from Guler himself after 30 minutes.
Jude Bellingham played the ball out to the flank where record signing Diomande received it and fed Guler on the edge of the box.
The Turkish playmaker lofted a superb strike across Sevilla goalkeeper Odysseas Vlachodimos and into the top corner.
- Mbappe skill -
Mbappe came close to adding a second with a lightning-quick burst down the pitch, but his low effort was saved.
The French superstar soon got his goal, one of the best of the season.
Bellingham backheeled the ball into Mbappe's path and the forward produced a dazzling roulette turn into the area, before showing more skill to rapidly sidestep the goalkeeper and roll home.
Sevilla complained that striker Robbie Ure was fouled in the build-up, to no avail.
Mbappe extended the lead from the penalty spot after he went down under a light touch from Andres Castrin in the area.
The forward, who hopes to be crowned the best player in the world at the Ballon d'Or ceremony later in October, dinked home his ninth league goal of the season.
Sevilla pulled one back with a neat strike from Manuel Bueno, but there was no fightback on the cards.
Ivorian winger Diomande thumped home from outside of the box for his second goal since joining this summer from RB Leipzig, Madrid's next opponents in the Champions League.
Earlier, Real Sociedad rose to fifth with a thumping 5-2 win at bottom side Malaga, Celta Vigo defeated Alaves 2-1 and Osasuna beat Racing Santander 2-0.

item.title: Arsenal snatch late win to keep pressure on City as Man Utd held
item.description:
Arsenal struck late to beat Nottingham Forest and keep the pressure on Premier League leaders Manchester City on Sunday, while struggling Manchester United dropped more points in a draw at Leeds.
The Gunners faced Forest a day after pacesetters City celebrated a seventh win in seven games at home to Ipswich -- shrugging off the fallout from the club's guilty verdict for serious financial irregularities.
Defending champions Arsenal huffed and puffed against Oliver Glasner's struggling side but finally secured the breakthrough when substitute Noni Madueke's effort found the net in the 80th minute after a deflection off Jair Cunha.
The goal was Arsenal's only shot on target in a disjointed performance that lacked attacking quality, but they are showing an impressive ability to grind out results when not at their best.
The 1-0 victory moved Mikel Arteta's side back up to second in the table, three points behind leaders City, while Forest, who failed to capitalise on a clutch of late chances, are now in the relegation zone.
"We had to earn it until the last second," Arteta told the BBC. "They are a well-coached team and hard to break down.
"We had to take risks, they are a dangerous team. We had to manage the emotional part really well. We stayed focused and the finishers made a huge impact."
Earlier, Manchester United travelled to the home of bitter rivals Leeds desperate to find a spark but were forced to settle for a 1-1 draw after Dominic Calvert-Lewin cancelled out Bryan Mbeumo's first-half opener.
United have just one win in seven league games this season and are winless in their past six matches in all competitions.
Manager Michael Carrick -- in his first full season in charge -- is scrambling for answers, with his team looking short of quality and confidence.
The sense of a growing crisis at Old Trafford was exacerbated by a midweek outburst from defender Lisandro Martinez, who took aim at the United hierarchy after a 2-0 defeat at Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.
Carrick chose to focus on the positives after Sunday's game at Elland Road, insisting that the draw was a step in the right direction.
"If there's any weakness, it gets found out today," he told Sky Sports.
"I could feel before the game that the players were ready for it. It wasn't perfect, our confidence isn't sky-high, but the players were trying to do the right things.
"In moments we looked really good. Defended really well as a team."
Argentina centre-back Martinez gave an explosive interview in Spain on Tuesday during which he criticised the lack of investment in the summer transfer window.
Carrick insisted on Friday that United had "moved on" from the incident and Martinez was named in the starting line-up.
Mbeumo, playing as United's target man, wasted a couple of chances but broke the deadlock in the 35th minute when he guided a Youri Tielemans cross into the bottom corner for his fourth goal of the season.
Leeds put the visitors under sustained pressure after the break and were level in the 51st minute when England forward Calvert-Lewin controlled the ball on his chest and finished at full stretch after Tarik Muharemovic's header from a corner.
United, 13th in the table, have their fewest wins at this stage of a top-flight campaign since 1986/87.
Elsewhere on Sunday, Brighton hammered Crystal Palace 5-0, including a sensational Diego Gomez effort from the halfway line.
Only three sides in Premier League history have scored more goals in their first seven games of a season than Brighton's haul of 23.
Bournemouth beat 10-man Sunderland 2-0 with goals from Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson for their first league win of the season.

item.title: Houthi attack on Yemen govt camp kills over 30
item.description:
A Houthi attack killed more than 30 people and wounded at least 70 others on Monday when three ballistic missiles struck a military camp in Yemen’s oil-rich Shabwa province, two military sources told AFP.
The government sources said the missiles hit the al-Alam camp, used by forces aligned with Yemen’s internationally recognized government, amid renewed fighting with the Iran-backed Houthis after the collapse of a truce that had largely held since 2022.
Majed al-Nuzaili, spokesperson for the Yemeni armed forces, wrote on X that the “Houthi militia targeted Shabwa with three ballistic missiles.”
He said the attack hit a training center for members of the security and police services.
A government military source in Shabwa said the army feared the strikes could pave the way for a ground offensive “similar to what happened in Mocha,” when the Houthis seized the strategic port city on Yemen’s Red Sea coast near the Bab al-Mandab strait.
The source, who requested anonymity, added that the Houthis cut a road linking government-held Shabwa with Houthi-controlled Al-Bayda province on Sunday, with locals saying they had been prevented from using the route.

item.title: US embassies urge ‘heightened vigilance’ in Middle East
item.description:
US embassies across much of the Middle East urged Americans to increase their vigilance on Monday, citing a “complex security environment” and travel disruptions eight months into the US-Iran war.
Embassies in the Gulf, Israel, Iraq, Lebanon and Jordan issued a security alert saying: “Americans currently in the Middle East should exercise heightened vigilance due to the complex security environment.”
“Be aware of potential flight cancellations, airspace closures, and travel disruptions.”
The warning cited attacks by Yemen’s Houthis on Saudi Arabia, where Riyadh’s international airport remains closed after 18 people were killed in a string of strikes this month.
“The hostilities have the potential to escalate rapidly beyond that immediate area,” the warning said, urging US citizens to monitor flight information and prepare contingency plans.

item.title: Indonesia fires have burned nearly two million hectares
item.description:
Fires in Indonesia that have caused a regional haze crisis burned through over 1.9 million hectares between January and the end of September this year, a monitor analyzing satellite imagery said on Monday.
The new figures came as Indonesian officials rebuffed calls to declare the fires a national disaster and said the country was “still capable of handling the situation ourselves” after neighboring Malaysia again offered assistance.
New figures from deforestation monitoring site Nusantara Atlas showed an area nearly 12 times larger than London has burned this year in Indonesia, the bulk of it as drought took hold from June, exacerbated by a strong El Nino cycle.
Indonesia’s government has not provided official figures for areas burned since announcing 202,000 hectares had been razed by the end of July.
Nusantara Atlas founder David Gaveau said the true scale of the burning was likely to be even higher than the 1,916,588 hectares his organization has detected so far.
“Our burned-area estimates are conservative for two reasons. First, we exclude individual burn scars smaller than 6.25 hectares... Second, we prioritize avoiding false detections,” he said.
This year, the calculation has also been impacted by heavy haze, which has obscured satellite images at times.
“The total reported burned area therefore underestimates the true area burned,” he said.
Even so, Nusantara Atlas data shows the area burned by the end of September this year was 38 percent higher than the same point in 2019.
The satellites the monitor uses were not available during severe fires in 2015, so comparable data is not available.
But Gaveau said it was likely this year would be similarly bad.
“My intuition is that it probably is as bad. If you look at the sheer number of hotspots, it’s still trending up and up,” he said.
Indonesia’s forestry ministry did not immediately respond to AFP’s request for comment on the figures.
Indonesia experiences fires every dry season, but this year’s blazes have been particularly severe, sickening hundreds of thousands of people locally and spiking air pollution in neighboring countries.
The haze has prompted school closures in Malaysia and East Timor, with haze drifting into Singapore and as far afield as the Philippines.
Singapore’s National Environment Agency (NEA) confirmed Monday that the number of consecutive days in which air quality dipped into “unhealthy” levels has surpassed that of 2015, when the region experienced its worst haze crisis.
By Monday, there had been 15 consecutive days classed as “unhealthy” based on the local PSI air quality measuring system, exceeding the eight measured in 2015, NEA deputy director Jason Evan Tan told AFP.
Singapore classes a day as “unhealthy” if the local PSI measure tips over 100 at any point during the day.
A separate analysis by AFP data journalists showed Monday was the 15th consecutive day on which the average PSI across Singapore hit over 100 at any hour of the day, though overall haze levels were lower than last week.
Singapore sent warnings to three more companies on Monday, urging them to take action against the fires, the NEA said.
It followed notices sent to seven other Indonesian companies on Friday, telling them to deploy fire-fighting teams, stop burning or starting new fires, and submit their action plans to the NEA.
“Since then, there are indications that smoke from fires in Kalimantan on lands held via concessions under three additional companies in Indonesia could have moved to Singapore,” the NEA said in a statement.
Indonesia insisted Monday it did not need foreign help fighting the blazes.
“It is not a question of whether assistance is available,” said Coordinating Minister for Political and Security Affairs, Dudung Abdurachman
“For the time being, however, we are still capable of handling the situation ourselves.”

item.title: Police ‘lost control’ during French protests, says interior minister
item.description:
French police “lost control” during nationwide protests marred by violence over the weekend, the interior minister admitted Monday, with President Emmanuel Macron calling for a security review.
Macron also refused Interior Minister Laurent Nunez’s resignation even as he acknowledged security and intelligence failures in the government response.
Saturday’s demonstrations saw some half a million people turn out across France to protest the cost of living, but morphed into some of the worst violence to rock the country in years, with town halls and shops looted and set ablaze.
More than 2,500 people were arrested, while almost 1,000 members of the security forces were injured. Injuries were also reported among protesters, with one demonstrator’s hand blown off by a police crowd-control grenade.
“On Saturday, in some major cities, you couldn’t look shopkeepers in the eye after hundreds of shops had been looted and tell them we hadn’t lost control,” Nunez said.
Nunez acknowledged a “lack of anticipation” in the deployment of security forces on Saturday, whose numbers were insufficient to deal with the large crowds of rioters and looters on the fringes of the demonstrations.
He estimated that some 60,000 law enforcement personnel had been deployed across the country that day.
“Given the damage that has been caused, it was only right that I should hand in my resignation,” Nunez said.
The presidency said in a statement that Macron had rejected the resignation, however, citing “the necessity for continued leadership of law enforcement.”
Instead, Macron ordered Nunez to “take all necessary steps to ensure transparency over the failures in planning and intelligence that led to the violence.”
To end the “barricades and looting, he also requested that the interior minister promptly implement new operational methods for security forces to use on the ground in combating rioters,” the statement added.
Looting continued on Sunday, with Paris Mayor Emmanuel Gregoire saying Monday that around 30 shops had been targeted in the capital the previous day, describing the scenes as “unbearable.”
Nunez said some 350 people had been arrested in Paris on Sunday and overnight.
Nationwide, more than 2,330 people were taken into police custody over the weekend, 70 percent of whom were adults, Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin said Monday.
More than 2,000 shops were expected to have been affected by the weekend’s violence across France, with damage running into “hundreds of millions of euros,” according to chamber of commerce president Alain Di Crescenzo.
In an address to the nation Sunday evening, Macron slammed the “unbridled” violence and said local authorities would be able to ban -- “if necessary” -- certain rallies in coming days.
But he stopped short of announcing drastic measures, such as a state of emergency or curfew.
Saturday’s protests followed four weeks of high school student protests that at times also turned violent.

item.title: ‘A Bed, A Home and Graves’
item.description:
Kalakendra in Lalmatia is currently hosting A Bed A Home and Graves , a photography and video installation by Ahmed Rasel, curated by Wakilur Rahman. The exhibition opened on Friday, 9 October, with economist Anu Muhammad and photographer Saiful Huq Omi, principal of Counter Foto, as guests.
It stays open to the public until 26 October, so visitors have a little over a week left to see it.
Photo: Dhaka Tribune
Rasel’s work comes from a place he knows personally. He was born in southern Bangladesh, a region exposed to rising seas and river erosion.
In 1997, his grandparents lost their home and all their land to the river. As a child, he watched his grandmother age in a new city, grieving for what the water had taken.
That experience, he says, shaped how he understands the loss of collective memory and well-being among climate-affected communities, and it is why he approaches environmental issues “from a deeply embodied perspective.”
Photo: Dhaka Tribune
The exhibition reflects a shift in his practice. After more than a decade of documentary photography and teaching, Rasel has spent the past three years moving beyond conventional documentary storytelling.
He now builds large-scale, site-specific installations using local materials and spatial strategies, moving from distant observation towards intimate engagement. The aim, he says, is to let photography work with emotional urgency and extend into three-dimensional, sculptural forms.
Photo: Dhaka Tribune
His earlier projects, The Fish Was Kept Alive to Tell the Story and Memories of Lost Lands , blend archival material with contemporary images and treat water as both nurturer and destroyer.
Rasel’s work has been shown at Dhaka Art Summit (2018 and 2023), Chennai Photo Biennale (2021), Kolkata International Photo Festival (2019), KALA South Asia, among others. It has been published in outlets including Art Monthly UK, Trouw , Private Magazine and F-stop .
A Bed A Home and Graves runs until 26 October at Kalakendra, 9/3, Block-D, Lalmatia, Dhaka 1207. The exhibition is open to all, daily from 4pm to 8pm.

item.title: Mercantile Bank, Epic Health Care sign MoU for exclusive healthcare discounts
item.description:
Mercantile Bank PLC and healthcare institution Epic Health Care Ltd have officially signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to strengthen professional ties and extend exclusive healthcare benefits to the bank's stakeholders.
The agreement was signed by Md Shaiful Alam Chowdhury, regional head of the bank’s Chattogram Region, and TM Hannan, executive director of Epic Health Care Ltd, on behalf of their respective organizations.
The signing ceremony was graced by branch managers of all Chattogram regional branches of Mercantile Bank, along with senior officials from Epic Health Care Ltd.
The overall event was coordinated by Anupam Kumar Paul, official from the Chattogram Regional Recovery Division.
Under this partnership, Mercantile Bank’s debit card, credit card, and Mastercard holders, as well as all bank officers and their family members, will be able to access premium healthcare services at preferential rates.
To make healthcare more affordable, the agreement features some special discounts such as 30% discount on all pathology tests, 25% discount on all radiology, ultrasound, cardiac tests, and neurology tests, additional healthcare facilities and benefits as per the agreement terms.
This strategic alliance is expected to further foster mutual professional goodwill and commercial collaboration, ensuring enhanced well-being and accessible medical care for the bank’s customers, employees, and their families.

item.title: Durga Puja: PM Tarique Rahman to visit 3 divisions in a day to greet devotees
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will visit Rangpur, Rajshahi and Chattogram tomorrow, Tuesday to visit Durga Puja mandaps outside the capital and exchange greetings with the Hindu community people on the occasion of their biggest religious festival.

He will visit one puja mandap in each of the three divisions and extend greetings to devotees celebrating Sharadiya Durga Puja, Additional Press Secretary to the Prime Minister Atikur Rahman Rumon told BSS today, Monday.

"The Prime Minister will visit three districts to see the puja mandaps. He will first go to Rangpur in the morning, followed by Rajshahi and Chattogram," he said.

Rumon said this would be the first time a head of the government in Bangladesh would visit Durga Puja mandaps outside the capital during the Hindu community's biggest religious festival.

During the visits, the Premier will exchange greetings and speak with devotees, he added.

Tarique Rahman is scheduled to leave Tejgaon Airport in Dhaka by military aircraft at 9:00 am tomorrow, Saturday.

According to the tour schedule, he will fly to Saidpur Airport and visit either the Dharmasabha or Radha Govinda Temple in Rangpur.

He will then fly to Rajshahi's Hazrat Shah Makhdum (R) Airport and visit Rajshahi Dharmasabha Temple at 1:30 pm.

After a brief stay at the Rajshahi Circuit House, he will address a public rally at the city's historic Madrasa ground at 3:00 pm.

From Rajshahi, the Prime Minister will travel to Shah Amanat International Airport in Chattogram.

In the evening, he will visit the puja mandap at JM Sen Hall in Rahmatganj before staying at the Chattogram Circuit House.

He is scheduled to return to Dhaka by air at night, the Additional Press Secretary said.

The Prime Minister visited puja mandaps in the capital's Mohakhali and Banani areas last night. His wife, Dr Zubaida Rahman, accompanied him during the visits.

Tuesday is Maha Navami, the penultimate day of Sharadiya Durga Puja. The festival will conclude the following day with the immersion of the idols.

item.title: Let’s work shoulder to shoulder to build Bangladesh, regardless of faith: PM
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman today, Monday called upon people of all faiths to work together, shoulder to shoulder, to build Bangladesh, saying that every citizen has equal rights in the country regardless of religious identity.

“This country belongs to you, and this country belongs to me. Let us all work together, shoulder to shoulder, to build the country,” he said while addressing the Hindu community people during a visit to Dhakeshwari National Temple in the capital on the occasion of Durga Puja this evening.

He was accompanied by Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed and Social Welfare Minister Prof Abu Zafar Md. Zahid Hossain, said PM’s Assistant Press Secretary KM Nazmul Haque.

Stressing that the state belongs to everyone irrespective of religion, Tarique Rahman said people may practise different faiths, but all citizens enjoy equal rights and the state is responsible for ensuring their security.

“Religion may be different for you and me, but the state belongs to all of us. In Bangladesh, you have rights just as I do, and you have duties towards the country just as I do,” he said.

The Prime Minister said the state had a responsibility to ensure the security of every citizen, while people also had a shared responsibility to look after one another and work together to take the country forward.

“We are all children of this country and Bangladeshis. We are all human beings. This is our foremost identity. Everyone present here is a Bangladeshi,” he said.

Recalling the Liberation War of 1971, Tarique Rahman said people had fought for the country's independence without distinguishing between Muslims, Hindus, Buddhists and Christians.

“During the Liberation War, when people took to the battlefield to win the sun of freedom, we did not see who was Muslim, Hindu, Buddhist or Christian. We never asked such questions,” he said.

He said people from all faiths had also stood together in subsequent movements to restore democracy and voting rights, without asking about one another's religious identities.

The Prime Minister recalled the mass uprising of August 5, 2024, saying people from different religious communities had joined the movement to establish people's rights.

“It was not long ago. It has not even been two and a half years. On 5 August 2024, thousands and hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets. Did any of us ask anyone which religion they belonged to?” he said.

Referring to the martyrs of the July uprising, he said people from Hindu, Muslim, Buddhist and Christian communities had sacrificed their lives for establishing people's rights.

The premier said he had earlier inaugurated the July Martyrs Memorial at Osmani Udyan in the capital today, where people from different religious communities were among those honoured.

Calling for collective efforts to bring about development and positive change in the country, Tarique Rahman said the benefits of progress would be shared by everyone.

“If this country changes and the lives of its people improve, you will benefit just as I will,” he said, adding that people should recognise one another as fellow human beings and citizens of Bangladesh.

Extending greetings to members of the Hindu community on Durga Puja, the Prime Minister described the occasion as a celebration of joy and a gathering that brings people together.

item.title: Former JCD leader ‘Shooter’ Lelin arrested in Chattogram
item.description:
The Detective Branch (DB) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police has arrested Abul Kalam Azad, also known as Lelin, former convener of Shah Ali Thana unit of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD), on charges of involvement in an incident of attack, vandalism, and looting at Radda Health Centre in the capital’s Mirpur.

He was arrested from Chattogram early this morning, Monday. He is listed in police records as “Shooter Lelin”.

The incident of attack, vandalism, and looting took place at Radda Health Centre in Mirpur late one night last month.

Mohammad Rakibul Islam, Deputy Commissioner (DC) of the DB, told Prothom Alo that Abul Kalam Azad was arrested on specific charges of involvement in the attack on Radda Health Centre.

The court has granted a two-day remand to interrogate him, he added.

item.title: Ishraque defends armed anti-drug operation, speaks about mayoral election
item.description:
Ishraque Hossain has defended the actions that drew widespread criticism and ultimately led to his resignation as state minister. The ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) lawmaker announced at a press conference that he had resigned as State Minister for Liberation War Affairs at the direction of the Prime Minister.

At the same event, he sought to justify his participation in an anti-narcotics operation while brandishing a firearm. He also answered journalists’ questions on a range of issues, including the upcoming city corporation election.

On Sunday, a day after footage of Ishraque taking part in an anti-narcotics operation in Gandaria, in the capital, with a firearm in his hand went viral on social media, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman summoned him and asked him to step down as state minister.

At a press conference at the National Press Club in Dhaka on Monday afternoon, Ishraque announced his resignation.

“As of today, I have voluntarily sought release from my responsibilities as State Minister for the Ministry of Liberation War Affairs from the honourable Prime Minister,” he said, adding that the prime minister had agreed to his request.

Ishraque began the press conference by giving a lengthy account of the incident, repeatedly insisting that his actions had been justified.

After announcing his resignation, he took several questions from journalists, who asked him about various aspects of the controversy.

Asked about the law and order situation and why he had conducted his own “operation” despite the presence of government security forces, Ishraque said law enforcement agencies had not fully returned to normal operations following 5 August 2024. In those circumstances, he said, they had been compelled to take certain initiatives themselves after six or seven months.

He added that, after repeatedly approaching various law enforcement agencies without achieving the expected results in improving security in Dhaka, he had discussed the matter with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.

Ishraque said his parliamentary constituency comprised 11 wards covering Sutrapur, Wari and Gandaria, as well as parts of Bangshal and Kotwali police station areas in Dhaka.

He said they held meetings at least once a month with the officers-in-charge of the relevant police stations, the deputy commissioners of the Lalbagh and Wari divisions of Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP), and traffic officials to discuss law and order, traffic congestion and other local problems.

As an MP, he said, they had been entrusted with addressing minor problems in their constituencies. The prime minister did not need to visit every alley personally to issue instructions on such matters.

“He is the head of the Cabinet. He definitely will give directions,” Ishraque said.

He claimed that he had discussed the issues with the prime minister, explained his position and requirements, and that the prime minister had immediately instructed the relevant authorities to act.

Referring to the period after 5 August 2024, Ishraque said three police stations in his constituency had been set on fire, leaving them virtually without facilities. He said they had arranged seating and furniture for police personnel to enable them to resume their duties.

He added that they believed in the rule of law and continued to work in the interests of the country and its people. They had fulfilled their responsibilities while in opposition, he said, and now wanted to play an even more active role.

At the press conference, Ishraque also claimed that confusion had arisen over the timing and process of news reports about the prime minister’s directive.

In response to journalists’ questions, he said an official decision was supposed to be communicated through the prescribed process. However, one of his colleagues had disclosed the matter before the scheduled time, creating confusion.

Ishraque argued that until the prime minister’s directive was formally announced, reports about it should be treated as rumours or false information. He said he had received the formal decision on Monday morning.

“Does it really matter whether it happened yesterday or today? It happened,” he said.

Will contest mayoral election if party decides

A journalist asked Ishraque whether he was now considering running for mayor.

In response, he said the decision rested entirely with the Bangladesh Nationalist Party and its leader, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.

“I have said that the mayoral election is entirely within the jurisdiction of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party and our honourable Prime Minister, Tarique Rahman, and will be decided solely by him,” Ishraque said.

He noted that he had contested the mayoral election in 2020 and had gained electoral experience. He had also been working on various urban problems for a long time in accordance with his party’s directives, he added.

Ishraque identified the lack of central planning, poor coordination among different agencies and various structural weaknesses as some of Dhaka’s major problems. He said he had been working on these issues for years.

If the party decided to nominate him for the election, he would be fully prepared to contest, he said. However, if the party chose someone else, he would make every effort to ensure that candidate’s victory.

Asked whether he believed he had been the victim of a political conspiracy leading to his resignation, Ishraque denied that any political party had conspired against him.

However, he said he had been hurt by a remark made by a leader of Jamaat-e-Islami, the principal opposition party. The leader had accused him of committing acts of violence by brandishing a firearm, Ishraque said.

“How else am I supposed to explain what I went there to do in broad daylight, with the police present and hundreds of people around? Some 300 grams of heroin, several bottles of alcohol and many other illegal items were recovered there,” he said.

“I went there putting my life on the line. Many people say that about me, although I do not care about it. If someone fires from a rooftop, we do not know whose head the bullet might hit. Even so, when I hear this kind of allegation from them instead of assurances of support, I feel that I should no longer look in that direction,” Ishraque added.

The MP also said he had witnessed the public’s response to the operation.

“I have seen what ordinary people want. That day, the local residents and members of the public were literally applauding and celebrating. After a long time, we have regained our courage. I will continue working in line with their expectations,” he said.

Although Ishraque repeatedly highlighted the applause he said he had received from local residents, his actions have drawn widespread criticism. Political analysts have described the episode as a striking example of a display of power, immaturity and arrogance.

Writer and researcher Mohiuddin Ahmad believes the government’s reputation has suffered because of what he sees as Ishraque’s lack of maturity and sound judgement.

After the press conference, Ishraque left the third floor of the Press Club building surrounded by party activists, who chanted various slogans in his support. He later got into his vehicle and waved to the supporters.

With the vehicle’s roof open, he also delivered a brief address to the crowd through a handheld microphone, reiterating his resignation.
